newsitem.title: USA: Ohio school funding plan action expected this week.
newsitem.headline: Ohio school funding plan action expected this week.

text.p: Ohio lawmakers anticipate possible committee votes this week on the proposed overhaul of the state's public school funding system, a spokeswoman for House Speaker Jo Ann Davidson said Monday.

The Senate finance committee is expected to take up the measure this week, while representatives have not decided if they will vote a substitute plan this week or await receipt of the bill, spokeswoman Cheryl Burchard said.
Representatives have inserted some fiscal accountability language into the proposal while senators have provided for some academic accountability, Burchard said.
Lawmakers have agreed not to include a proposed constitutional amendment making the Ohio General Assembly the final arbiter of deciding what is fair and equitable in funding, Burchard said.
Ohio Supreme Court justices in March overturned the state's school funding formula and gave lawmakers one year to overhaul the system.

A task force appointed by Gov. George Voinovich has recommended increasing state aid by $1.1 billion in the the current biennium and providing $5.8 billion for capital improvements over the next 10 years.

The task force recommended financing the plan by raising the state sales tax from 5 percent to 6 percent, increasing the cigarette tax and lifting the property taxes on businesses and commercial properties.
The plan requires lawmakers to approve placing three constitutional amendments on the November ballot by August 6.
